items.purpose: Pursuant to the provisions of H. Res. 1275, the amendment in the nature of a substitute recommended by the Committee on the Judiciary, printed in the bill, modified by the amendment printed in Part A of House Report 119-648, is considered adopted.

dimensions.assessment: Affects court-appointed monitors, state and local government entities subject to consent decrees or settlement agreements, federal judges, and the public.
dimensions.evidence: monitoring the conduct of a State or unit of local government.

dimensions.assessment: Imposes strict structural limitations on monitorships, including fee caps, term limits, mandatory case reassignments after six years, and public accounting requirements.
dimensions.evidence: may not be appointed for a term greater than 5 years; or reappointed after the expiration of such term pursuant to the same court order.

dimensions.assessment: The source does not provide federal spending or macroeconomic data, though it caps monitor fees.
dimensions.evidence: may not assess a fee in excess of such maximum rates as the Judicial Conference of the United States may establish

dimensions.assessment: Directs the Judicial Conference of the United States to establish nationwide rules governing federal district court monitor appointments.
dimensions.evidence: the Judicial Conference of the United States shall by rule establish conditions on the appointment by a district court

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent rules for federal court appointments and includes retroactive provisions for existing long-standing monitorships.
dimensions.evidence: In the case of a monitorship that is in effect on the date of enactment of this Act and has been in effect for 6 years

missing_information: Estimates of administrative savings or impacts on court operations.
importance_detail.rationale: Requires the Judicial Conference to establish conditions on court-appointed monitors overseeing state and local governments, including fee caps, 5-year term limits, public comment periods, annual accountings, and case transfers after 6 years.
